aarti.tek: Om, victory to you, bearer of the axe; Lord, victory to you, bearer of the axe. Gods, men and sages serve you, the incarnation of Viṣṇu, the Lord of Śrī.
aarti.pad1: You are the son of Jamadagni, a lion among men, born of mother Reṇukā. You are radiant as the sun, a descendant of Bhṛgu; your fame has spread over the three worlds. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: On your shoulder is the sacred thread, around your neck a rosary of rudrākṣa; wooden sandals grace your feet, and the three-lined tilaka, the tripuṇḍra, marks your forehead. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: Your thick hair is a coppery dark, and matted locks are bound up on your head. To the good you are a season full of sweetness, to the wicked a storm that crushes them. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: The radiance of the sun shines on your face, and your eyes are red. You are the protector of the lowly and helpless, of cows and brahmins, day and night. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: The excellent axe shines in your hand; you know the Vedas and the āgamas. On your shoulder are Viṣṇu’s bow and arrows; you are the protector of the brahmin line. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: You are my mother, father, master, friend and companion. Uphold my honour; I lie at your door. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: Whoever sings the āratī of the ageless, deathless Śrī Paraśurāma — Pūrṇendu says it with Śiva as his witness — gains happiness and wealth. ॥7॥
